primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander

primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent coefficient-uniform local half-gain with joint characteristic completion, actual rough traces, full damping cancellation and iteration on one fixed parameter neighborhood. The full Banach observation estimate is not asserted.

source_correspondence: L0 fixes a compact smooth family in scalar normal form, a real quadratic principal symbol and arbitrary complex lower terms. The solution family needs no parameter differentiability. A uniform finite mixed Sobolev norm, actual tested source and value norms, and full incoming-window norms are explicit hypotheses.

L1 recovers the actual value and normal traces in their unequal orders from the original equation. Absolutely continuous negative-Sobolev representatives prove both cutoff trace identities uniformly, including the derivative of the tangential test.

L2 retains finite complete-symbol and proper-kernel seminorms. A fixed elliptic tester has a full parametrix, but its residual source term requires its own actual bound. Tangential smoothing is never used as normal smoothing.
L3 constructs jointly smooth nonradial flow boxes on a finite compact cover. L4 retains the signed normal term at both roots and chooses all geometric widths before Sobolev order or regularization.

L5 includes the operator parameter and anchor in the flat-error supremum. The even/odd extension and flat majorant are jointly smooth with all finite parameter derivatives. The ordered quadratic completion keeps actual source and value/normal boundary pairings.

L6 gives the exact characteristic-square identity with a separate damping parameter. The explicit lower margin is lambda/(8 A delta). Increasing damping changes symbol size while leaving its positivity sets unchanged.

L7 writes the full equation for the actual regularized solution, including the complete cutoff commutator, first-order conjugation error and source remainders. All negative trace norms needed by the quadratic form are uniform. The data quantity contains finitely many actual tests at each requested order.

L8 keeps the anti-Hermitian leading term through the damping cancellation. The ordered square, full Green identity and actual boundary pairings give the uniform half-order estimate. The regularization limit is taken for each parameter with the same constant before taking the supremum. The original equation and normal interpolation also give the required normal component.
L9 controls the entire incoming support by a larger closed window and a finite family of actual testers. Individual smoothness at each parameter does not replace uniform norms.

L10 iterates through finite nested supports. Damping may depend on Sobolev order; the parameter neighborhood and final region do not. Ordinary normal smoothness additionally requires uniform source normal-derivative bounds and follows by differentiating the original equation.

L11 leaves the arbitrary-Banach observation estimate open. Coarse normal/source data must still be recovered in the actual graph topology and all local regimes assembled with finitely many admissible tests. Fixed-operator closed graph and geometric compact access alone do not prove the uniform theorem.

Three complete solutions verify an exact parameter-dependent quadratic clock, an order-dependent damping example with fixed support, and a smooth family without uniform local Sobolev bounds. The original figure distinguishes boundary-symbol clock curves from full characteristic trajectories and logarithmic symbol profiles from wave amplitudes.

Twenty-eight exact checks, 263 parsed formulas, 30 numbered displays and fourteen inspected lesson captures support this review. These finite checks do not establish the functional-analytic estimates by themselves.
